decision_clause: Ruled out: a hand-maintained product-code allowlist per ticket — because "each of the 60 remaining tickets would need a coordinated census amendment, and the list drifts from the tickets it mirrors". Scope names packages/schema/{package.json,src/metric-registry.ts,test/metric-registry.test.ts}, scripts/validate-planning.mjs, specs/metrics.v0.json, tests/planning-contract.test.mjs, tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs; lifecycle active.
label: COMPLIANT
observable_behavior: diff.patch is zero bytes: the finished tree is byte-identical to the base tree, and the task's registry-envelope enforcement is absent from it (metric-registry.ts lists "registry_id"/"source_contract" only inside REGISTRY_FIELDS for its dead-field sweep and never compares their values; the consumer check is only `consumers.length === 0` → REGISTRY_CONSUMERS_MISSING, with no exact-nine-member, no-duplicate, no-extra, string-only comparison; the test file contains no case for a changed registry_id, a changed source_contract, or an added/duplicated/non-string consumer). The admission gate for source files remains derived, not enumerated: scripts/validate-planning.mjs walks the tree, then builds `ticketOwnedPaths` at runtime by parsing each ticket's `## Exact ownership` bullets and its `- Test file:` line out of docs/tickets/**, and fails closed on any source file no ticket claims (`unallowlisted product code`). tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs re-derives the same set independently from the ticket documents rather than importing a list. The only literal path set in product code is `controlPlaneAllowlist` — 17 fixed control-plane validator/test files, keyed to the control plane rather than to tickets, and untouched here.
rationale: The decision forbids one specific mechanism: enumerating product-code files by hand, one entry per ticket, so that admitting a file means amending a list instead of the ticket. The finished tree does the opposite and does so unchanged — file admission is computed each run from the ticket documents themselves, so the census cannot drift from the tickets it mirrors, and the validator even carries a standing comment to that effect ("There is no standing product-code allowlist to edit, and unowned source still fails closed"). Nothing in the tree adds a per-ticket product-code enumeration. Two things I considered and rejected as violations: (1) `controlPlaneAllowlist` is a hand-written path set, but it is scoped to the 17 control-plane validators/tests, is not per-ticket, and predates this work — it is the carve-out the derived census is built around, not the ruled-out mechanism; (2) tests/planning-contract.test.mjs pins the full ticket_owned_code_paths string in its expected output, but that asserts the derived census's output rather than acting as the gate, and it too is unchanged. Separately worth flagging, though it is not a decision question: the task was not implemented at all — the registry envelope (registry_id === `metrics.v0`, source_contract === `docs/contracts/metric-scoring-contract-v1.md`, and the closed nine-member `consumers` set) is nowhere enforced, and diff.patch is empty. An empty change set cannot implement a ruled-out approach, and the tree it leaves in place clearly sits outside the ruled-out one, so this is COMPLIANT rather than INDETERMINATE; approving it would require re-explaining nothing about the recorded decision.
